meta.title: Evomon Adventure Suits data

dropRates.note: Drop chances per rarity for the Adventure Suit gacha. Use these for per-section notes at the writing stage (keyed by section label). Normal Spin = 2,000 Coins; Lucky Spin = Robux or passes.

imageCoverage.note: No genuine per-suit in-game icon renders are available from accessible sources. The only complete per-suit image set found (Pro Game Guides tier list, /wp-content/uploads/2026/06/<Suit>.jpg) is text-label name tiles (the suit name on a flat colored background), not actual in-game suit artwork, so it was rejected per the no-placeholder rule. Sportskeeda lazy-loads only two menu/building screenshots, not per-suit icons; Gamezebo 403s; community Dex wikis (evomon.wiki, evomon.org, evomon.app) are client-rendered with no scrapable suit icons and no dedicated suit pages. All 22 suits are accepted-missing and render text-first; the dataset is otherwise complete and the page works without images.

sources.label: Pro Game Guides - Evomon Adventure Suit Tier List
sources.usage: Primary roster: full 22-suit list with canonical suit names, rarities, and exact buff text. Used for canonical naming (e.g. Normal Novice, Capture Experts, Physical Expert, Monster Hunter, Elemental Mage).

sources.label: Sportskeeda - Evomon Adventure Suit guide
sources.usage: Independent confirmation of all 22 suits, rarities, and effects, plus obtaining mechanics (NPC Debby gacha, Normal Spin 2,000 Coins, Lucky Spin Robux/passes, 6-slot storage) and per-rarity drop rates for normal and lucky spins.

sources.label: Gamezebo - All Evomon Adventure Suits [Buffs, Rarities, How to Get]
sources.usage: Cross-check of buffs, rarities, and obtaining notes (direct fetch 403; verified via search summaries).

sourceNotes: Roster is 22 Adventure Suits across six rarities: Uncommon (2), Rare (4), Epic (6), Legendary (5), Mythic (3), Eternal (2). Confirmed independently by Pro Game Guides and Sportskeeda with matching names, rarities, and buffs.

Suit name variants were normalized to the most complete source (Pro Game Guides): 'Normal' -> 'Normal Novice', 'Capture' -> 'Capture Experts', 'Physical' -> 'Physical Expert', 'Monster' -> 'Monster Hunter', 'Elemental' -> 'Elemental Mage', 'Treasure' -> 'Treasure Hunter'. Sportskeeda short forms are not rendered.

Commander 'Lead vs Last' wording: Pro Game Guides says 'Lead Evomon's Elemental Skill Damage +8%'; Sportskeeda says 'Last Evomon'. Sources conflict, so effect text uses neutral wording ('one team slot's elemental skill damage +8%') rather than asserting Lead or Last. Resolve in-game if possible before publish.

effectCategory is a derived helper field (Movement, Skill Damage, Capture, Economy, Survivability, Healing, Utility) to let players compare what each suit improves. It is not a source label; it summarizes the source-backed effect.

collectionSection holds the rarity-tier section label ('<Rarity> Suits'). rarity holds the bare rarity word for the highlight chip. The two are intentionally duplicated: collectionSection drives grouping, rarity drives the per-card highlight.

Drop rates (per rarity, normal and lucky spin) are stored in meta.dropRates for the writing stage to render as per-section notes, not per-card fields. They are stable but balance-patchable; keep as supporting context, not the page's core promise.
Images are deferred to the image gate (all null now); not a data blocker.
Evergreen-safe: no dates, no 'current/latest/updated', no active-count-as-freshness wording in any rendered prose field.

items.name: Runner
items.effect: Increases player movement speed by 25%.
items.cardSummary: Runner is a pure overworld-mobility suit that makes your character move 25% faster, so traveling between areas and reaching battles is quicker. It does nothing in combat, so most players swap it out once they have a damage or capture suit.

items.name: Normal Novice
items.effect: Increases Normal-type skill damage by 5%.
items.cardSummary: Normal Novice adds 5% skill damage for Normal-type Evomon only, so it helps teams built around Normal attackers. Its narrow scope and small bonus make it an early-game filler until a wider damage suit drops.

items.name: Fire Novice
items.effect: Increases Fire-type skill damage by 5%.
items.cardSummary: Fire Novice gives 5% extra skill damage to Fire-type Evomon, making it a cheap pick for Fire-leaning teams. It only helps that one element, so its value depends entirely on how many Fire attackers you run.

items.name: Water Novice
items.effect: Increases Water-type skill damage by 5%.
items.cardSummary: Water Novice adds 5% skill damage to Water-type Evomon, a budget boost for Water-focused teams. Like the other Novice suits, it scales only with how much of your team shares that element.

items.name: Grass Novice
items.effect: Increases Grass-type skill damage by 5%.
items.cardSummary: Grass Novice raises Grass-type skill damage by 5%, helping teams that lean on Grass attackers. It is an early-game element suit you typically replace once a broader damage option appears.

items.name: Capture Experts
items.effect: Increases capture success rate by 5%.
items.cardSummary: Capture Experts improves your capture success rate by 5%, so wild Evomon are slightly easier to catch. It is an entry-level catching suit that the Epic Catch Master later outclasses.

items.name: Treasure Hunter
items.effect: Increases coins earned from battles by 15%.
items.cardSummary: Treasure Hunter adds 15% to the coins you earn from battles, speeding up everything coins buy, including more gacha spins. It is a strong farming suit when you are grinding currency rather than pushing combat power.

items.name: Breeder
items.effect: Increases Evomon EXP earned from battles by 10%.
items.cardSummary: Breeder grants 10% more Evomon EXP from battles, so your team levels faster while you grind. It is a leveling suit best worn during EXP farming rather than tough fights.

items.name: Catch Master
items.effect: Increases capture success rate by 10% and capture chance by 1.
items.cardSummary: Catch Master is the dedicated capture suit: +10% capture success and one extra capture attempt per encounter. It is the go-to choice when you are hunting and taming new Evomon.

items.name: Vanguard
items.effect: Increases first-turn damage by 22%.
items.cardSummary: Vanguard adds a large 22% bonus to damage on the first turn of a battle, rewarding fast, aggressive openers. It shines in short fights where you can win on the opening burst but does nothing after turn one.

items.name: Primal Mage
items.effect: Increases Fire, Water, and Grass skill damage by 5% each.
items.cardSummary: Primal Mage rolls the three elemental Novice bonuses into one suit, adding 5% skill damage to Fire, Water, and Grass attackers. It is a flexible damage option for mixed elemental teams that use the core three types.

items.name: Commander
items.effect: Increases one team slot's elemental skill damage by 8%.
items.cardSummary: Commander gives a focused +8% elemental skill damage to a single team-slot Evomon, so it rewards building around one strong elemental carry. Sources disagree on whether the slot is the lead or last Evomon, so confirm placement in-game before relying on it.

items.name: Physical Expert
items.effect: Increases Physical skill damage by 8%.
items.cardSummary: Physical Expert adds 8% damage to all Physical skills, regardless of element, making it a broad pick for Physical-attack teams. It pairs naturally with Evomon whose strongest moves are physical rather than special.

items.name: Special Expert
items.effect: Increases Special skill damage by 8%.
items.cardSummary: Special Expert mirrors Physical Expert for Special moves, granting 8% to all Special skill damage across elements. It is the better damage suit for teams that rely on special attackers.

items.name: Monster Hunter
items.effect: Increases Evomon EXP from battles by 10% and capture success rate by 15%.
items.cardSummary: Monster Hunter doubles as a leveling and catching suit: +10% battle EXP and +15% capture success in one slot. It is efficient for players who are both grinding levels and expanding their collection at the same time.

items.name: Elite Hunter
items.effect: Increases damage dealt to bosses by 11%.
items.cardSummary: Elite Hunter adds 11% damage specifically against bosses, making it a top pick for boss fights and raids. It does nothing against normal enemies, so it is a situational swap for tough encounters.

items.name: Guardian
items.effect: Reduces damage taken from bosses by 11%.
items.cardSummary: Guardian is Elite Hunter's defensive counterpart, cutting damage taken from bosses by 11% so your team survives longer in hard fights. It is most valuable on boss encounters where survival, not extra damage, is the bottleneck.

items.name: Elemental Mage
items.effect: Increases skill damage by 2% for each unique element in your party.
items.cardSummary: Elemental Mage scales with team variety, adding 2% skill damage for every unique element on your party, so a rainbow team gets the most out of it. It rewards diverse rosters and is weak on mono-element teams.

items.name: Mediator
items.effect: Allied Evomon take 8% less damage from the enemy lead Evomon's elemental type.
items.cardSummary: Mediator is a defensive suit that cuts 8% of the damage your team takes from the enemy lead's element, softening type-disadvantage matchups. Its value depends on the opposing lead's element, so it shines against predictable elemental threats.

items.name: Pharmacist
items.effect: Potions restore 20% more HP to allied Evomon.
items.cardSummary: Pharmacist boosts potion healing by 20%, stretching your healing items further in long fights and grinds. It is a sustain-focused suit that pairs well with potion-heavy playstyles rather than burst damage.

items.name: Energy Scholar
items.effect: Increases Ultimate skill damage by 16%, grants +1 initial Ultimate energy, and recovers 1 energy after each Ultimate used.
items.cardSummary: Energy Scholar is widely rated the best suit: it boosts Ultimate damage by 16%, starts you with extra Ultimate energy, and refunds energy after each Ultimate, so you use powerful Ultimates more often. It is the standout choice for Ultimate-driven teams.

items.name: Champion
items.effect: Increases all skill damage by 11%.
items.cardSummary: Champion adds a flat 11% to all skill damage with no conditions, so it helps every Evomon on any team. That universal, build-free bonus makes it one of the most beginner-friendly top-tier suits.
